uncited: Topological Correctness Guarantees is a family of isosurface extraction methods designed to resolve the topological ambiguities inherent in standard Marching Cubes [Marching Cubes](774-marching-cubes.md).

Standard Marching Cubes uses linear interpolation, which can produce incorrect connectivity (e.g., disconnected sheets instead of a tunnel) when the underlying trilinear interpolant has critical points within a voxel [Topologically Correct Marching Cubes](1368-topologically-correct-marching-cubes.md).

This family ensures the output mesh is homeomorphic to the trilinear interpolant of the input scalar field or a valid 2-manifold for binary data, preventing non-manifold artifacts and self-intersections [Topologically Defined Isosurfaces](1428-topologically-defined-isosurfaces.md).

Unlike standard implementations that rely on arbitrary lookup tables, these methods use geometric tests, vertex insertion, or global connectivity constraints to deterministically resolve ambiguous configurations [Asymptotic Decider](790-asymptotic-decider.md)[Topologically Defined Isosurface via Connectedness Couples](1430-topologically-defined-isosurface-via-connectedness-couples.md).

This typically occurs when a face has alternating signs (a saddle) or when the interior of the cube contains a critical point [Asymptotic Decider](790-asymptotic-decider.md)[Topologically Correct Marching Cubes](1368-topologically-correct-marching-cubes.md).

Resolution strategies vary: geometric tests evaluate the bilinear interpolant on ambiguous faces [Asymptotic Decider](790-asymptotic-decider.md); vertex insertion adds anchors (e.g., at the cell center) to resolve interior tunnels [Topologically Correct Marching Cubes](1368-topologically-correct-marching-cubes.md); connectivity constraints enforce valid foreground/background couples for binary data [Topologically Defined Isosurfaces](1428-topologically-defined-isosurfaces.md); and higher-order interpolation uses Hermite data or averaged face values [Marching Cubes with Hermite Data and Full Case Table](961-marching-cubes-with-hermite-data-and-full-case-table.md).

This requires handling degenerate cases (e.g., $Q=0$) and ensuring that shared edges between adjacent voxels are triangulated consistently [Topologically Correct Marching Cubes](1368-topologically-correct-marching-cubes.md)[Topologically Defined Isosurface via Connectedness Couples](1430-topologically-defined-isosurface-via-connectedness-couples.md).

The problem of topological ambiguity in Marching Cubes was first identified by Lorensen and Cline (1987), who proposed 15 unambiguous cases, leaving 18 ambiguous cases unresolved [Marching Cubes](774-marching-cubes.md).
Natarajan (1995) provided a rigorous test for these ambiguities using the trilinear interpolant [Asymptotic Decider](790-asymptotic-decider.md).
Subsequent work by Chernyaev (MC33) and others expanded the lookup tables to handle all 33 topological cases [Extended Trilinear Triangulation](1618-extended-trilinear-triangulation.md).

For binary volumes, combinatorial topology approaches by Coeurjolly et al. established the use of connectedness couples to guarantee manifold surfaces [Topologically Defined Isosurfaces](1428-topologically-defined-isosurfaces.md).
Recent developments integrate these guarantees into differentiable rendering pipelines using consistency losses [Topology/Normal Consistency Loss](4351-topology-normal-consistency-loss.md).
